The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 09.02.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 09.02.2021 at about 5.30 pm the Petitioner was riding Suzuki Access Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA07EB 6581 along with one Smt.Roopavathi slowly carefully and cautiously observing all traffic rules and regulations.
At that time all of a sudden a Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA05AH 9979 which was driven by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner dashed to his Suzuki Access.
Consequently, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar wherein first aid treatment was given and he was further shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
So far he has spent Rs.36,00,000/ towards medical and nourishment expenses.
The petitioner has sustained permanent disability.
He is not able to lead a normal life as prior to the said accident.
The petitioner has suffered loss of income due to this accident.
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, the accident is caused due to the reckless driving by the driver of the Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA05AH9979.
The Kolar Rural Police has registered a case against the driver of the vehicle.
The 1st respondent is the insurer and the 2nd respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence both are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
4. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent No.1 appeared and filed written statement.

In spite of due service of notice the Respondent No.2 did not appear hence, placed Ex parte.
5.

The objections of the Respondent No.1:
It has admitted the policy issued in favour of the Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA05 AH9979 and liability to indemnify the 2nd respondent.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further contended that the driver of the Tempo Goods vehicle was not holding valid and effective DL and permit to ply as on the date Venkatesha P vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38644492/

The Respondent insurer has further denied the manner of accident, petitioner's age, occupation, income.

On the other side, the Respondent No.1 did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on its behalf.

18. The petitioner has averred that, at the time of accident he was doing Agriculture, Milk Vending and earning Rs.25,000/ per month.

Therefore, the court deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 20%.

The accident took place in the year 2021.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at R.L.Jalappa Hospital,
Kolar and thereafter he was treated at Manipal Hospitals, Bangalore wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 10.02.2021 to 08.03.2021, conducted surgery and discharged with advice to take follow up treatment.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.9 Discharge summary issued by Manipal Hospital, Bangalore.
Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.36,00,000/ towards hospitalization,
medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.13 for a sum of Rs.20,61,312/. During the cross examination of PW.4
, he has stated

that as per Ex.P.21 out of Rs.19,78,092/ only Rs.7,44,999/
was received from the petitioner.
In addition the petitioner got admitted to the hospital again from 27.11.2022 to 29.11.2022 and spent Rs.1,21,809/ as per Ex.P.23.
Therefore, the total medical expenses of the petitioner comes to Rs.9,49,028/.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment at RL Jalappa hospital and Manipal Hospital, Bangalore for 26 days which can be made out from Exs.P.8 & 9 Discharge summaries of the said hospitals.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.23,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
On perusal of Ex.P.10, as on the date of accident he was 58 years old.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable for his age is 9.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.2,48,400/ (Rs.11,500/ x 12 x 9 x 20%= Rs.2,48,400/) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 56 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 20% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/

(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo Two more operations for removal of implants from Bilateral superior pubic rami and right sacro iliac joint.
In this regard the petitioner or the PW.2 have not produced any estimation bills.

Therefore, looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

23. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.60,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.9,49,028/
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.23,000/ period 4. Loss of future income Rs.2,48,400/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/ happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges
7. Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/ TOTAL Rs.13,40,428/
If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.13,40,500/ and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY 24.
The Respondent No.1 in the written statement has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective DL, permit as on the date of accident.

It has contended that,
the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself but has not proved the same.
Therefore, the Respondents being the insurer and the Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.2/insured and to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.13,40,500/ with interest @ 6% per annum Venkatesha P vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38644492/

25. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues this court proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.13,40,500/ (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs Forty Thousand and Five Hundred only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.

On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% of amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
It has contended that,
the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself but has not proved the same.
Therefore, the Respondents being the insurer and the Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.2/insured and to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
